title: Psalms Chapter 59 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 59 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 59 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 59.

questions.question: Who is the Psalm 59 attributed to?
questions.explanation: Psalms 59:1 states it is a Michtam of David.

questions.question: What situation is described in Psalms 59:1 as the reason for the Psalm's writing?
options: When Saul sent men to kill David by watching his house
When David was lost in the wilderness
questions.correctAnswer: When Saul sent men to kill David by watching his house
questions.explanation: Psalms 59:1 says Saul sent and they watched the house to kill David.

questions.question: From whom does David ask God to deliver him in Psalms 59:2?
options: Workers of iniquity and bloody men
questions.correctAnswer: Workers of iniquity and bloody men
questions.explanation: Psalms 59:2 specifically requests deliverance from workers of iniquity and bloody men.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 59:3, David's enemies lie in wait for him because of his sin.
questions.explanation: Psalms 59:3 states they lie in wait not for his transgression or sin.

questions.question: What does David ask God to do in Psalms 59:4?
options: Awake to help him and behold
questions.correctAnswer: Awake to help him and behold
questions.explanation: Psalms 59:4 says, 'awake to help me, and behold.'

questions.question: Who is addressed as 'God of hosts' in Psalms 59:5?
questions.explanation: Psalms 59:5 calls on the LORD God of hosts, the God of Israel.

questions.question: True or False: In Psalms 59:5, David asks God to be merciful to the wicked transgressors.
questions.explanation: Psalms 59:5 says, 'be not merciful to any wicked transgressors.'

questions.question: At what time do David’s enemies return and make noise according to Psalms 59:6?
questions.explanation: Psalms 59:6 states they return at evening and make a noise like a dog.

questions.question: How are the enemies’ sounds compared in Psalms 59:6?
questions.explanation: Psalms 59:6 says they make a noise like a dog.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 59:1 is a prayer for deliverance from enemies who rise up against David.
questions.explanation: Psalms 59:1 asks for deliverance from enemies that rise up against David.

questions.question: What does David say about his enemies in Psalms 59:3 regarding their reason for attacking him?
options: They are not attacking for any sin or transgression
They attack because of his sins
They attack because of a dispute over land
questions.correctAnswer: They are not attacking for any sin or transgression
questions.explanation: Psalms 59:3 clearly states the enemies are not attacking for his transgression or sin.

questions.question: In Psalms 59:2, which kind of men does David specifically ask to be saved from?
questions.explanation: Psalms 59:2 requests deliverance from bloody men.

questions.question: Which of the following comes first in Psalms 59?
options: Asking God to awake to help
Calling God the God of Israel
Requesting God to be merciful to wicked transgressors
questions.correctAnswer: Asking God to awake to help
questions.explanation: Psalms 59:4 (asking God to awake to help) comes before verses 5 and 6 which mention God as God of Israel, mercy, and enemies making noise.

questions.question: True or False: In Psalms 59:6, the enemies go round about the city.
questions.explanation: Psalms 59:6 says they go round about the city like dogs.

questions.question: What is David's plea to God regarding the wicked transgressors in Psalms 59:5?
options: Be not merciful to any wicked transgressors
questions.correctAnswer: Be not merciful to any wicked transgressors
questions.explanation: Psalms 59:5 specifically asks God not to be merciful to wicked transgressors.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 59 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 59 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 59:7, how do the enemies express themselves?
options: They belch out with their mouth and have swords in their lips
They remain silent and watch carefully
questions.correctAnswer: They belch out with their mouth and have swords in their lips
questions.explanation: Psalms 59:7 clearly states that the enemies 'belch out with their mouth' and 'swords are in their lips,' indicating their harsh and threatening speech. This is supported by the hostile imagery found in Psalms 59:6 and the derision mentioned in Psalms 59:8.

questions.question: What is God's response to the enemies according to Psalms 59:8?
options: He will laugh at them and hold all the heathen in derision
He will plead for their forgiveness
questions.correctAnswer: He will laugh at them and hold all the heathen in derision
questions.explanation: Psalms 59:8 tells us that God 'shalt laugh at them; thou shalt have all the heathen in derision,' showing divine confidence and sovereignty over the enemies. This contrasts with their hostile behavior in Psalms 59:7 and assures the believer of God's power.

questions.question: How does the psalmist describe his attitude toward God in Psalms 59:9?
options: He waits upon God because of His strength and defense
questions.correctAnswer: He waits upon God because of His strength and defense
questions.explanation: In Psalms 59:9, the psalmist expresses faith and trust by waiting upon God 'because of his strength' and acknowledges that 'God is my defence.' This trust follows God’s derision of enemies in Psalms 59:8 and precedes the merciful protection in Psalms 59:10.

questions.question: What does Psalms 59:10 teach about God's mercy and the psalmist's desire?
options: God will ignore the psalmist's enemies
God will prevent the psalmist and frustrate his desires
God will prevent the psalmist and let him see his desire upon his enemies
God will ask the psalmist to forgive his enemies immediately
questions.correctAnswer: God will prevent the psalmist and let him see his desire upon his enemies
questions.explanation: Psalms 59:10 shows that 'The God of my mercy shall prevent me' and will allow the psalmist to see his desire upon his enemies, implying divine protection and vindication. This complements the trust expressed in Psalms 59:9 and the derision of enemies in Psalms 59:8.

questions.question: What does Psalms 59:11 caution about the manner of dealing with enemies?
options: Slay them immediately to ensure safety
Slay them not, lest my people forget; scatter and bring them down by God's power
questions.correctAnswer: Slay them not, lest my people forget; scatter and bring them down by God's power
questions.explanation: The verse advises 'Slay them not, lest my people forget,' suggesting that God’s power should be displayed by scattering and bringing down enemies rather than outright killing them. This connects with the mercy in Psalms 59:10 and the divine defense in Psalms 59:9.

questions.question: According to Psalms 59:12, why should the enemies be taken in their pride?
options: Because of their kindness and generosity
Because of the sin of their mouth, words of their lips, cursing, and lying
questions.correctAnswer: Because of the sin of their mouth, words of their lips, cursing, and lying
questions.explanation: Psalms 59:12 explains that the enemies should be caught in their pride due to 'the sin of their mouth and the words of their lips,' particularly cursing and lying. This reveals the nature of their hostility, which is addressed by God’s justice as described in Psalms 59:11 and the mercy in Psalms 59:10.

questions.question: How does the psalmist instruct believers to respond to the enemies' pride and lies according to Psalms 59:11-12?
options: By killing them quickly and forgetting their offenses
By forgiving them without any consequences
By scattering them with God's power and letting their pride catch them
By ignoring their pride and lies
questions.correctAnswer: By scattering them with God's power and letting their pride catch them
questions.explanation: Psalms 59:11-12 teaches that the enemies should not be slain outright but scattered by God's power, and that their pride should be their downfall. This balanced justice ensures God's power and mercy are evident, contrasting with their sinful speech and cursing.

questions.question: What practical lesson about faith and waiting on God can be drawn from Psalms 59:9-10?
options: Faith requires immediate action without patience
Waiting on God is trusting His strength and mercy to defend and fulfill desires against enemies
One should rely on their own strength rather than God's
God will always remove enemies without effort
questions.correctAnswer: Waiting on God is trusting His strength and mercy to defend and fulfill desires against enemies
questions.explanation: Verses 9 and 10 emphasize waiting on God because of His strength and mercy, trusting Him for defense and vindication. This encourages believers to practice patient faith rather than relying solely on human effort, as shown by the psalmist's confidence.

questions.question: According to Psalms 59:8, what attitude does God have toward the heathen enemies?
questions.explanation: Psalms 59:8 states that God 'shalt laugh at them; thou shalt have all the heathen in derision,' indicating a mocking and sovereign attitude toward the enemies, showing their impotence against Him.

questions.question: Based on Psalms 59:11-12, what is the reason given for not slaying the enemies outright?
questions.explanation: Psalms 59:11 explains that the enemies should not be slain 'lest my people forget,' indicating that their defeat should be a testimony to God's power. This is linked to the sins of their speech mentioned in verse 12, which justifies their scattering rather than immediate destruction.

questions.question: How does Psalms 59:7 suggest the enemies believe others respond to their threats?
options: They believe everyone fears and obeys them
They think no one listens to their threats
They assume forgiveness will be granted
questions.correctAnswer: They think no one listens to their threats
questions.explanation: Psalms 59:7 ends with 'for who, say they, doth hear?' showing the enemies' arrogance that their threats go unheeded. This highlights their false confidence, contrasting with the divine response in Psalms 59:8.

questions.question: What is the significance of the instruction in Psalms 59:11 when connected with the sin of the enemies' speech in Psalms 59:12?
options: To encourage believers to ignore enemies' words
To highlight that justice includes exposing pride and lies without killing
To suggest revenge is the best response
To teach that silence is the best defense
questions.correctAnswer: To highlight that justice includes exposing pride and lies without killing
questions.explanation: Psalms 59:11 advises against killing enemies outright to ensure their pride and lies (Psalms 59:12) are exposed and remembered. This teaches believers about measured justice and the power of God's intervention over personal vengeance.

questions.question: Based on Psalms 59:9-12, how does this passage teach about trusting God in times of conflict?
options: Trusting God means immediate and total destruction of enemies
Trusting God involves waiting on His strength, seeking His mercy, and allowing Him to control the outcome
Trusting God requires ignoring enemies completely
Trusting God means handling matters personally without prayer
questions.correctAnswer: Trusting God involves waiting on His strength, seeking His mercy, and allowing Him to control the outcome
questions.explanation: These verses show the psalmist’s trust in God’s defense and mercy (verses 9-10), and instruct believers to let God scatter enemies (verse 11) and expose their sinful speech (verse 12), demonstrating faith in God's sovereign control rather than personal vengeance.

questions.question: If a believer is struggling with resentment toward an enemy who lies and curses, based on Psalms 59:11-12, what biblical truth should they apply?
options: They should trust God to scatter the enemy and expose their pride without killing
They should ignore the situation completely
They should retaliate with similar lies
questions.correctAnswer: They should trust God to scatter the enemy and expose their pride without killing
questions.explanation: Psalms 59:11-12 teaches that God will scatter enemies and bring down their pride and lies, encouraging believers to trust God’s justice and mercy rather than seeking personal revenge, which promotes faith and humility.

questions.question: What does Psalms 59:7-8 imply about the ultimate outcome for those who threaten with lies and pride?
options: They will succeed and intimidate others
God will laugh at them and hold them in derision
Their threats will be ignored, but they will remain powerful
questions.correctAnswer: God will laugh at them and hold them in derision
questions.explanation: Verses 7 and 8 contrast the enemies’ proud threats with God's response of laughter and derision, showing that God does not fear them and will ultimately humiliate them, teaching believers about God's sovereign protection.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 59 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 59.

questions.question: What is the psalmist's request regarding the enemies in Psalms 59:13?
options: Consume them in wrath so they may not be
Let them prosper in the land
questions.correctAnswer: Consume them in wrath so they may not be
questions.explanation: Psalms 59:13 explicitly requests God to 'Consume them in wrath, consume them, that they may not be,' showing a plea for divine judgment against the enemies.

questions.question: According to Psalms 59:13, what is the purpose of consuming the enemies?
options: So they may know God rules in Jacob unto the ends of the earth
So they may repent and return
So they may be exalted before God
questions.correctAnswer: So they may know God rules in Jacob unto the ends of the earth
questions.explanation: The verse states that consuming the enemies will let them know that 'God ruleth in Jacob unto the ends of the earth,' emphasizing God's sovereign reign.

questions.question: What imagery is used in Psalms 59:14 to describe the enemies returning at evening?
options: Making a noise like a dog and going around the city
Singing like birds in the morning
Running like lions through the fields
questions.correctAnswer: Making a noise like a dog and going around the city
questions.explanation: Psalms 59:14 describes the enemies as making a noise like dogs and circling the city in the evening, a metaphor for their persistent threat.

questions.question: In Psalms 59:15, what behavior is attributed to the enemies wandering for meat?
options: They grudge if they are not satisfied
questions.correctAnswer: They grudge if they are not satisfied
questions.explanation: The verse says the enemies 'let them wander up and down for meat, and grudge if they be not satisfied,' indicating their restless and dissatisfied nature.

questions.question: What does the psalmist promise to do in the morning according to Psalms 59:16?
options: Sing aloud of God's mercy and power
questions.correctAnswer: Sing aloud of God's mercy and power
questions.explanation: Psalms 59:16 states, 'I will sing aloud of thy mercy in the morning' and also sing of God's power, showing praise and trust in God.

questions.question: What titles does the psalmist use for God in Psalms 59:17?
options: My strength, my defence, and the God of my mercy
The King of kings and Lord of lords
questions.correctAnswer: My strength, my defence, and the God of my mercy
questions.explanation: The psalmist declares God as 'my strength,' 'my defence,' and 'the God of my mercy' in Psalms 59:17, emphasizing divine protection and mercy.

questions.question: Which other biblical passage shares a similar theme of God ruling over all nations as in Psalms 59:13?
questions.explanation: Psalm 2:8 speaks of God’s sovereign rule over the nations, which aligns with Psalms 59:13's theme of God's rule over Jacob and the ends of the earth.

questions.question: What literary device is exemplified by the repetition of the enemies making noise 'like a dog' in Psalms 59:6 and 59:14?
questions.explanation: The repetition of the imagery of dogs making noise at evening at both the start (verse 6) and near the end (verse 14) of this section forms an inclusio framing the enemies’ behavior.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'Selah' likely signify as seen in Psalms 59:5 and 59:13?
questions.explanation: 'Selah' is thought to indicate a pause or musical interlude in the psalms, suggesting a moment to reflect on the preceding words, as in Psalms 59:5 and 59:13.

questions.question: What reason does the psalmist give in Psalms 59:11 for not wanting God to slay the enemies outright?
questions.explanation: Psalms 59:11 says, 'Slay them not, lest my people forget,' indicating a desire for God’s power to be remembered rather than enemies being simply killed.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God as the defender and refuge in trouble, as in Psalms 59:16?
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 4:18 speaks of the Lord rescuing and defending from evil, echoing Psalms 59:16's theme of God as refuge in trouble.

questions.question: In Psalms 59:12, for what sins are the enemies to be taken in their pride?
options: Sin of their mouth and words of their lips, cursing and lying
questions.correctAnswer: Sin of their mouth and words of their lips, cursing and lying
questions.explanation: The verse specifies the enemies' sins as 'the sin of their mouth and the words of their lips,' including cursing and lying, which bring judgment upon them.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 59 was written by David when Saul sent men to watch his house to kill him.
questions.explanation: The superscription in Psalms 59:1 states it is 'a Michtam of David; when Saul sent, and they watched the house to kill him,' confirming David as the author and the historical context.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist calls for mercy upon the wicked transgressors in Psalms 59:5.
questions.explanation: Psalms 59:5 says, 'be not merciful to any wicked transgressors,' indicating a call for judgment rather than mercy on the wicked.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage shares a similar motif of God laughing at the nations, as in Psalms 59:8?
questions.explanation: Psalm 2:4 says, 'The Lord shall laugh at them,' paralleling Psalms 59:8 where God laughs at the nations in derision.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 59 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 59 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What is the primary request made by David in Psalms 59?
options: To be delivered from his enemies
questions.correctAnswer: To be delivered from his enemies
questions.explanation: David's main plea is for deliverance from his enemies as expressed in Psalms 59:1 where he says, 'Deliver me from mine enemies, O my God.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 59, what does David call the men who seek to harm him?
questions.explanation: David specifically refers to his adversaries as 'the workers of iniquity' in Psalms 59:2, highlighting their sinful actions.

questions.question: What does David imply about the nature of the enemies' actions in Psalms 59:3?
options: They are justified in their actions
They lie in wait for his soul
questions.correctAnswer: They lie in wait for his soul
questions.explanation: In Psalms 59:3, David states that his enemies 'lie in wait for my soul,' indicating their malicious intent and premeditated harm.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted in Psalms 59:9 where David expresses his reliance on God?
questions.explanation: David acknowledges God's protective nature in Psalms 59:9, stating, 'for God is my defence,' which emphasizes God’s power to protect.

questions.question: What does David ask God to do to his enemies in Psalms 59:11?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 59:11, David requests that God 'scatter them by thy power,' indicating a desire for God's intervention against his foes.

questions.question: In Psalms 59:13, what does David ask God to consume regarding the enemies?
questions.explanation: David prays for God to consume the enemies for 'the sin of their mouth and the words of their lips' which reflects their pride in Psalms 59:12-13.

questions.question: What does Psalms 59:5 reveal about God’s stance toward the wicked?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 59:5, David calls upon God to 'awake to visit all the heathen,' indicating that God will hold the wicked accountable.

questions.question: What metaphor does David use to describe his enemies in Psalms 59:6?
questions.explanation: David describes his enemies as making noise 'like a dog' in Psalms 59:6, emphasizing their disruptive and aggressive nature.

questions.question: How does David express his confidence in God in Psalms 59:10?
questions.explanation: David expresses confidence in God's strength by stating, 'Because of his strength will I wait upon thee' in Psalms 59:10.

questions.question: What theme does Psalms 59:16 convey regarding David's response to God's mercy?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 59:16, David declares, 'But I will sing of thy power,' indicating his response of praise for God’s mercy and protection.

questions.question: What does Psalms 59:14 imply about the persistence of David's enemies?
questions.explanation: Psalms 59:14 describes the enemies returning at evening, indicating their relentless pursuit of David.

questions.question: What doctrinal teaching is found in Psalms 59:17 regarding God's nature?
questions.explanation: David acknowledges God as 'the God of my mercy' and 'my defence' in Psalms 59:17, illustrating God's protective and merciful nature.

questions.question: What is the overall message of Psalms 59 regarding divine protection?
options: God helps those who help themselves
questions.explanation: The psalm emphasizes God's active role in defending David amidst adversity, affirming that God provides protection to those who seek Him.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the God of the Old Testament is unjust and unmerciful. What does Psalms 59:5-6 actually teach?
options: God does not defend His people
questions.explanation: Psalms 59:5-6 reveals God's judgment against the wicked and His active role in defending His people, showing that He is just.

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 11 and 12 convey about the consequences of wickedness?
options: The mouth's sin leads to pride and downfall
There are no consequences for sin
questions.correctAnswer: The mouth's sin leads to pride and downfall
questions.explanation: Verses 11 and 12 together highlight how the sins 'of their mouth' and 'the words of their lips' lead to their pride and consequent downfall.
